# ND-120

ND-120, 64-bit word (version K register selects)

- **Name for `%#MODEL` and the settings:** `nd120`
- **Also accepted:** `nd-120`
- **Word width in the bit view:** 64 bits
- **Image written by *Assemble*:** .CODE, 10-byte records
- **Ending of the image file:** `.CODE`
- **Mnemonics:** 358
- **Colours shared with:** ND-100, ND-110 and ND-120
- **Definitions:** [`defs/tokens/nd120-tokens.yaml`](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/defs/tokens/nd120-tokens.yaml)

## How the bits are given

The word is four groups of 16 bits: `w4` (bits 63-48), `w3` (47-32), `w2` (31-16) and `w1` (15-0), each written as 6 octal digits. Groups that are all zero are left out of the tables below. A mnemonic sets the bits that are 1 in its groups; the mnemonics of one instruction are ORed together.

## Fields of the word

The fields below are the ones this variant defines itself. The other fields are those of `nd110-fields.yaml`; see the page of that variant.

| Field | Bits | Width | Description | Used when | Default |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `ALUI` | 63:55 | 9 | ALU Function Select (full 9 bits on ND-120) |  | 0 |

### ROM bit flip

From the definitions, key `rom_bit_flip`.

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `applies_to` | ND-120 |
| `description` | ND-120 EPROM images have bits 22-27 inverted vs the assembled form |
| `mask` | 0x0FC00000 |
| `operation` | xor |
| `purpose` | When reading raw EPROM contents (e.g. from 45132L.bin + 45133L.bin), XOR with this mask to obtain the canonical assembled form used by the assembler and disassembler. When writing ROMs, apply the same XOR in reverse. |
